title: Lesson 11 - Writing Effective Prompts: Structure, Specificity, and Output Shape
description: Explain how to implement best practices for writing effective prompts.

questions.question: Which set names the three core elements of an effective prompt?
options: A clear task, relevant context, and a specified output format
A model, a temperature, and a token limit
A channel, a user, and a data space
A version, an object, and a field
questions.explanation: An effective prompt clearly defines the task, provides relevant context, and specifies the expected output format, and those three elements are the ones the guidance names as core.

questions.question: A prompt repeats the same customer facts in three places and the output comes back inconsistent. Which best practice does this violate?
questions.explanation: The reference-once principle says to name each fact a single time, because restating the same data in one prompt can lead to unexpected or inconsistent results, and grounding should supply the rest.

questions.question: A team needs every generated email to match their house tone and structure. Which technique should the writer use?
options: Add a longer role description with more adjectives
Raise the model temperature for variety
Remove all constraints so the model can adapt
Provide a few worked input and output examples so the model mimics the format and tone
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting gives the model worked examples of the task, which is the technique for making it mimic a particular tone, structure, or style, whereas adjectives and looser constraints do not set the pattern.
